ei.title: Chapter 6-17 1번: Positive Emotions and Creative Thinking
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: People tend to assume that positive emotions are sources of simplistic or lazy thinking. Think of any highly creative person — such as Vincent van Gogh, Virginia Woolf, T. S. Eliot, or Charles Darwin — and you imagine their creative acts were produced during moments of struggle, tension, gloominess, and even despair. Alice Isen suggested that this view of creativity is wrong — that happiness instead prompts people to reason in ways that are flexible and creative. In her studies, Isen induced positive emotion in her participants with small events. She gave them little bags of candy, or they found a dime she had placed in their path. They watched amusing film clips. These subtle ways of making participants feel good produced striking changes in their reasoning. When given one word (such as carpet) and asked to generate a related word, people feeling positive emotions came up with more novel associations (fresh or texture) than people in a neutral state, who tended to produce more common responses (such as rug). People feeling positive categorized objects in more inclusive ways, rating fringe members of categories (like cane or purse as an example of clothing) as better members of that category than people in a neutral state, whose categories tended to be more narrowly defined.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① flexible — induced — amusing: 행복이 사람들을 '유연한(flexible)' 방식으로 추론하게 하고, Isen이 작은 사건으로 긍정 감정을 '유도했으며(induced)', 참가자가 '재미있는(amusing)' 영상을 보았다는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ←정답
❌ ② rigid(경직된)는 '유연하게' 추론한다는 흐름과 반대
❌ ③ reduced(줄였다)는 긍정 감정을 '유도했다'는 설명과 반대
❌ ④ boring(지루한)은 '재미있는' 영상이라는 문맥과 반대

det.korean: ④ dull → amusing: 참가자들이 '재미있는(amusing)' 영상을 보았다는 문맥
det.analysis:
✅ ① simplistic — 긍정 감정이 '단순화된(simplistic)' 사고의 원천이라는 통념, 적절

det.korean: ① hide → generate: 관련 단어를 '만들어 내도록(generate)' 요청받았다는 문맥

det.korean: ② slight → striking: 미묘한 방법이 '두드러진(striking)' 변화를 낳았다는 문맥

Eliot, or Charles Darwin — and you imagine their creative acts were produced during moments of struggle, tension, gloominess, and even despair. Alice Isen suggested that this view of creativity is wrong — that happiness instead prompts people to reason in ways that are <u>flexible</u> and creative. In her studies, Isen induced positive emotion in her participants with small events. She gave them little bags of candy, or they found a dime she had placed in their path. They watched amusing film clips. These subtle ways of making participants feel good produced striking changes in their reasoning. When given one word (such as carpet) and asked to generate a related word, people feeling positive emotions came up with more novel associations (fresh or texture) than people in a neutral state, who tended to produce more common responses (such as rug). People feeling positive categorized objects in more inclusive ways, rating fringe members of categories (like cane or purse as an example of clothing) as better members of that category than people in a neutral state, whose categories tended to be more narrowly defined.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 flexible과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① adaptable: 적응력 있는 (flexible의 유의어)

❌ ③ gentle: 부드러운 (의미축이 다름)
❌ ④ smooth: 매끄러운 (관련 없음)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 reason의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ 추론하다 — 이유 ←정답
❌ ① 이유 — 추론하다 (A·B 순서가 반대)
❌ ② 추론하다 — 추론하다 (B는 '이유'이지 '추론하다'가 아님)
❌ ④ 이유 — 이유 (A는 '추론하다'이지 '이유'가 아님)
det.tip: reason: (A) 추론하다(동사, to think logically) vs (B) 이유(명사, cause)

det.korean: 이 '창의성(creativity)'에 대한 관점 — 전치사 of 뒤에 명사가 와야 한다.
det.analysis: this view of __________ (create) — 전치사 of의 목적어 자리이므로 명사가 필요 → creativity. create(동사: 창조하다)를 creativity(명사: 창의성)로 변환.
